Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) reflects non-enzymatic glycation of haemoglobin in proportion to mean plasma glucose across the erythrocyte lifespan; 8% corresponds to an estimated average glucose of roughly 183 mg/dL, which exceeds the usual goal of under 7% for most non-pregnant adults and indicates suboptimal glycaemic control that may warrant pharmacological intensification, for example metformin titration or the addition of a GLP-1 receptor agonist or SGLT2 inhibitor, alongside lifestyle modification and individualised targets.
